LLM auditresponse for haven-desktop-git.install:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The provided `.install` script performs standard post-installation, upgrade, and removal operations typical of an AUR package. The `post_install` function handles Electron sandbox permissions by conditionally setting the SUID bit on `chrome-sandbox` only when unprivileged user namespaces are not available — a well-documented requirement for Electron applications and consistent with upstream packaging practices. It creates a symbolic link to the binary in `/usr/bin` and manually triggers `gtk-update-icon-cache` to ensure the application icon is properly registered. This manual cache update is correctly justified in the comment: the pacman hook does not trigger because the package only adds files deep within an existing icon theme hierarchy, not at the top level.

All operations are confined to expected paths (`/opt/Haven`, `/usr/bin`, `/usr/share/icons/hicolor`) and serve the legitimate purpose of integrating the application into the system desktop environment. There are no network operations, file exfiltrations, obfuscated commands, or executions of external code. The use of `|| true` ensures that failures (e.g., missing sandbox binary) do not break installation, which is defensive but safe. The `post_upgrade` function safely reuses `post_install`, and `post_remove` cleanly removes the symlink.

This script reflects sound packaging practices with clear, transparent logic and no malicious indicators.
</details>
<evidence>
